chosen_display: Mishra's Bauble — {T}, Sacrifice {this}: Look at the top card of ta... [Activate]
annotation_description: With Nihil Spellbomb on the opponent's battlefield threatening to exile the graveyard, looking at your own library provides minimal value compared to scouting the opponent's top card. While the draw trigger happens regardless of target, seeing the opponent's top card gives information about their next draw, which is generally more useful since you'll see your own card when you draw it anyway. Additionally, there's no particular reason to prioritize knowing your own top card here.

Cast Thoughtseize before playing Swamp for the turn. By playing Swamp first, the player would have two black sources available and could potentially cast both Thoughtseize and Nethergoyf in the same turn. After Thoughtseize resolves, sorcery would be added to graveyard (alongside artifact from Mishra's Bauble), making Nethergoyf a 2/3 - a reasonable early play.

Took Engineered Explosives over Emry, Lurker of the Loch. Emry is the engine card that enables recurring Mishra's Bauble from graveyard for repeated card advantage, turns on Mox Amber by being legendary, and ties the opponent's artifact synergy strategy together. Engineered Explosives is more situational and requires specific mana to be effective.

By casting Nethergoyf before activating Nihil Spellbomb, the Nethergoyf enters as only a 1/2 (only sorcery in graveyard). If they had activated Nihil Spellbomb first (without paying {B} for the draw trigger), the Spellbomb would go to graveyard adding 'artifact' as a card type alongside 'sorcery', making Nethergoyf a 2/3 instead. Additionally, exiling the opponent's graveyard would deny potential Emry recursion of Engineered Explosives and Mishra's Bauble.

chosen_display: Nihil Spellbomb — {T}, Sacrifice {this}: Exile target player's grav... [Activate]
annotation_description: Activated Nihil Spellbomb when both black sources (Swamp and Ifnir Deadlands) were tapped, meaning Haiku Spike cannot pay {B} for the death trigger to draw a card. The opponent's graveyard (Mishra's Bauble and Engineered Explosives) isn't immediately threatening with no Emry on board.

Playing Otawara as a land instead of keeping it in hand sacrifices its channel ability (bounce an artifact/creature/enchantment/planeswalker). The basic Island provides the same mana, while Otawara in hand serves as flexible interaction that could bounce the opponent's Nethergoyf or other threats later.

Flame of Anor is arguably the more impactful card to take here. With Emry on the battlefield (a Wizard), Flame of Anor can choose two modes - it can draw 2 cards AND deal 5 damage to a creature (killing Nethergoyf or Thought-Knot Seer) or destroy an artifact. Cori-Steel Cutter is a 2-mana equipment that creates 1/1 tokens - it's decent but not immediately threatening. Flame of Anor is a 3-mana instant that represents a 2-for-1 with Emry out, and can remove Haiku Spike's key threats while replacing itself. However, there's a reasonable argument for taking Cori-Steel Cutter since it provides recurring value and the opponent has two copies, so the decision is debatable.

annotation_description: Chose Mishra's Bauble over Mox Opal with Emry's ability. Mox Opal is a permanent mana source that would provide ongoing mana advantage once Metalcraft is achieved (achievable this turn with Mox Amber + Mox Opal + Haywire Mite from hand). Mishra's Bauble only provides a delayed draw and is a temporary effect.

Casting a second Mox Amber when the first is already on the battlefield is wasteful due to the legendary rule - one will be sacrificed immediately. While this does put an artifact in the graveyard (useful for Emry), the player already has Mox Opal and other artifacts in the graveyard. The better play would be to play Urza's Saga first (as the land drop), then use Emry to tap and target an artifact in the graveyard (like Mox Opal or Mishra's Bauble), maximizing value. Playing a land before casting spells is generally correct sequencing, and Urza's Saga would begin accumulating lore counters and eventually create construct tokens or tutor for an artifact.

Gem25F Valley declined to activate Emry, Lurker of the Loch to target an artifact in the graveyard. The graveyard contains Mox Opal, Mox Amber, Mishra's Bauble, and Cori-Steel Cutter. With Emry on board plus Mox Amber, Haywire Mite, Mox Opal (in graveyard), and Urza's Saga as artifacts, activating Emry to cast Mox Opal from the graveyard would be free (metalcraft would be active with 4+ artifacts) and provide additional mana and artifact count for Urza's Saga constructs. Even casting Mishra's Bauble for free would be pure value (card draw next upkeep + graveyard fuel). There's no downside to tapping Emry to enable casting a 0-cost artifact from the graveyard.

Opponent has no creatures on the battlefield, so both Emry and Haywire Mite could attack with zero risk. Attacking with only Haywire Mite leaves 1 free damage on the table. If Emry's tap ability was needed, it should have been activated pre-combat.

Exiled Cori-Steel Cutter from hand, but there's already a copy in the graveyard that Emry can recur. Quantum Riddler (4/6 flyer with card draw, castable for {1}{U} via Warp) is the more impactful and irreplaceable threat.

Cast Kozilek's Command before playing Eldrazi Temple from hand. Eldrazi Temple produces {C}{C} specifically for colorless Eldrazi spells, and Kozilek's Command is a Kindred Instant — Eldrazi. Playing the land first would have added 2 additional mana (net +1 since Temple replaces a generic {C} source), allowing a significantly higher X value. This means more powerful modes - bigger exile targets, more tokens, deeper scry.

chosen_display: Emry, Lurker of the Loch — {T}: Choose target artifact card in your graveyar... [Activate]
annotation_description: Emry's activated ability lets you choose an artifact in your graveyard to cast this turn. Choosing Mishra's Bauble (a 0-cost artifact that draws a card next upkeep) is decent, but Mox Opal is already on the battlefield and two Mox Ambers are in the graveyard. With Emry (a legendary creature) on the battlefield, Mox Amber would tap for blue mana immediately, providing actual mana this turn. More importantly, casting Mox Amber would increase artifact count (boosting the Construct token) and provide mana to hold up Metallic Rebuke more easily. Mishra's Bauble doesn't draw until next upkeep and doesn't add to board presence this turn. However, the biggest consideration is that recasting Mox Amber for free gives an extra artifact for the Construct (which is already likely large) and mana, while Bauble's delayed draw is less impactful when the board is already developed.

Urza's Saga chapter III is searching for an artifact with mana cost {0} or {1} to put onto the battlefield. The opponent has a graveyard with Nethergoyf (which could escape) and other cards. Tormod's Crypt would provide graveyard hate to exile the opponent's graveyard, preventing Nethergoyf escape and weakening any future graveyard synergies. Mishra's Bauble is a cantrip that draws a card next upkeep, but Tormod's Crypt provides more strategic value given the opponent's graveyard-dependent threats. Additionally, the player already has Emry which can recur Mishra's Bauble from the graveyard later, making the Bauble less urgent to tutor for.

Failed to recognize that Mox Opal (with metalcraft from 3 artifacts: Haywire Mite, Construct Token, Mox Opal) can produce green mana to activate Haywire Mite's ability to exile the opponent's Urza's Saga, a high-value enchantment target. The player incorrectly believed they had no green mana available.

annotation_description: Chose scry+draw mode on Kozilek's Command instead of exiling Emry, Lurker of the Loch, the opponent's key value engine that recurs artifacts from the graveyard. Emry enables repeated Mishra's Bauble loops, Mox recursion, and other artifact synergies. Exiling it (permanently removing it rather than just destroying) would cripple the opponent's game plan.

Kozilek's Command on the stack is generating card advantage (scry + draw) and board presence (Eldrazi Spawn tokens) for the opponent. Gem25F Valley had Metallic Rebuke available and sufficient mana/artifacts to cast it (Mountain + Thundering Falls for {1}{U}, improvise one artifact for the third mana). The opponent likely couldn't pay {3} with their lands tapped from casting the Command.

Gem25F Valley could have used Mox Opal (metalcraft active with 3 artifacts) to produce green mana and sacrifice Haywire Mite to exile Urza's Saga in response to the chapter III trigger, denying Haiku Spike the artifact search. The reasoning incorrectly concluded they had no green mana source. Urza's Saga searches are high-value and denying it would be significant.

message: Select an artifact card with mana cost {0} or {1}
annotation_description: Urza's Saga Chapter III triggers a mandatory search for an artifact with mana cost {0} or {1} to put onto the battlefield. This is an extremely powerful effect. Haiku Spike declined to select any artifact, causing the Saga to be sacrificed for nothing. The search offered Shadowspear, Pithing Needle, and Mishra's Baubles. Shadowspear would be excellent as a legendary equipment giving +1/+1, trample, and lifelink to Thought-Knot Seer (making it a 5/5 with lifelink and trample after equipping). Pithing Needle could shut down Emry's activated ability, which is the opponent's key engine for recurring artifacts. Either choice would have been a significant advantage.

Should play Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth before casting Nethergoyf with Escape. With Urborg in play, Ifnir Deadlands and Eldrazi Temple both tap for black mana, giving {B}{B}{B} from lands + two Swamps, meaning the Eldrazi Spawn token doesn't need to be sacrificed to pay for Nethergoyf's {2}{B} escape cost. Casting Nethergoyf first likely requires sacrificing the Spawn token for colorless mana.

chosen_display: Emry, Lurker of the Loch — {T}: Choose target artifact card in your graveyar... [Activate]
annotation_description: Chose Mishra's Bauble over Mox Amber with Emry's ability. Mox Amber would stay on the battlefield as a permanent artifact, making the Construct token larger (+1/+1), providing blue mana via Emry being legendary, and giving an additional artifact for Metallic Rebuke's Improvise. Bauble gets sacrificed immediately and only draws a card next upkeep.

Cast Quantum Riddler before playing a land drop. Should play land first (Urza's Saga or Breeding Pool) to maximize available mana for the rest of the turn. While they have enough mana regardless, proper sequencing would leave more mana open for Metallic Rebuke or Unholy Heat after deploying the Riddler.

Cast Nethergoyf via Escape before playing their land drop (Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth). Playing Urborg first would make all lands Swamps, giving more black mana flexibility. Additionally, casting Inquisition of Kozilek first (after playing Urborg for additional mana) would reveal the opponent's hand to check for counterspells or tricks before committing to the Escape cost of exiling graveyard cards.

Chose Inquisition of Kozilek over Fatal Push when the opponent has a Construct Token on the battlefield that is likely 3/3 or larger (based on artifact count). The Construct represents immediate board pressure that should be addressed. Inquisition provides hand information but doesn't address the existing board threats.

Failed to cast Unholy Heat on Thought-Knot Seer when delirium is active (5+ card types in graveyard) and all opponent's lands are tapped. Unholy Heat would deal 6 damage to the 4/4 TKS, killing it and triggering its leave-the-battlefield ability which draws Gem25F Valley a card. This removes the biggest threat on the board while the opponent has no mana to respond.

Failed to activate Mishra's Bauble, which is a free ability (tap + sacrifice) that provides information and draws a card next upkeep. This is pure upside with no downside. The reasoning about 'saving it for upkeep' is incorrect - the draw always happens at the next upkeep regardless of when activated. Additionally, could have considered casting Unholy Heat (with delirium active for 6 damage) on Thought-Knot Seer while opponent was tapped out.

With delirium active (instant, creature, artifact, enchantment land in graveyard = 4+ types), Unholy Heat would deal 6 damage - enough to kill Thought-Knot Seer (4/4), the opponent's biggest threat. The player passed instead of removing it, leaving a 4/4 on board that was pressuring their life total. Thought-Knot Seer dying would also draw them a card.

chosen_display: Emry, Lurker of the Loch — {T}: Choose target artifact card in your graveyar... [Activate]
annotation_description: Targeted self with Mishra's Bauble peek instead of opponent. Looking at your own top card provides minimal value since you'll draw it anyway, while scouting the opponent's draw would help plan whether to hold up Metallic Rebuke or play proactively against Thought-Knot Seer and Nethergoyf.

With delirium active (5+ card types in graveyard), Unholy Heat deals 6 damage and can kill Thought-Knot Seer (4/4) or Nethergoyf while the opponent is completely tapped out and unable to respond. Passing up this opportunity to remove a major threat for just 1 mana is a significant missed play.

Pithing Needle is on the stack and will likely name Emry, Lurker of the Loch (their key engine piece for recurring artifacts from graveyard). While Haywire Mite could exile it later using Mox Opal for green mana, that costs a valuable creature. Metallic Rebuke with Improvise could counter it cheaply.

Fatal Push can legally target the Construct Token (mana value 0) which is a 5/5 threat. Instead, Haiku Spike targeted the 1/1 Haywire Mite. Killing the Construct removes 5 power from the opponent's board; killing Haywire Mite only reduces the Construct from 5/5 to 4/4 (one less artifact). With Haiku Spike at 12 life facing a Quantum Riddler (4/6) and Construct Token (5/5), removing the Construct is far more impactful for survival.

Haiku Spike attacked with only Thought-Knot Seer despite having Nethergoyf available. The opponent's only untapped blocker is a ~3/3 Construct Token, meaning attacking with both would guarantee at least 4 damage through (the unblocked creature). The reasoning even states the intent to attack with both creatures but only one was selected.

Blocked Nethergoyf (5/6) with the 4/4 Construct Token, which just chump blocks and dies without killing Nethergoyf, while Thought-Knot Seer (4/4) deals 4 damage unblocked. A much better line would be to block Thought-Knot Seer with the Construct (both die as 4/4 trades with 4/4), then use Unholy Heat with delirium (6 damage) to kill Nethergoyf, clearing both threats and taking 0 damage.

chosen_display: Emry, Lurker of the Loch — {T}: Choose target artifact card in your graveyar... [Activate]
annotation_description: Chose Haywire Mite over Mishra's Bauble with Emry's ability. Mishra's Bauble costs 0 mana (vs 1 for Mite), replaces itself with a card draw next upkeep, and immediately increases artifact count to pump the Construct token. While Haywire Mite can potentially exile the Pithing Needle, the Needle doesn't appear to be shutting down a critical ability (Emry's ability is currently working), making the free cantripping artifact the higher-value choice.

Using Unholy Heat on a 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn Token wastes a premium removal spell on a near-worthless target. The opponent can sacrifice the Spawn in response to add {C}, potentially fizzling the spell entirely. Even if it resolves, removing a 0/1 token is very low value for a card that can deal 2 (or 6 with delirium) damage to a real threat.

Emperor of Bones is a 2/2 that needs multiple turns to generate value (survive, adapt, reanimate temporarily), while Nethergoyf via escape would be an immediate 4/5 body. With 4 card types in graveyard (sorcery, instant, land, creature), Nethergoyf is a much more impactful threat. At 12 life vs opponent's 18, Haiku Spike needs to apply meaningful pressure quickly.

Attacking with Emperor of Bones (2/2) into an untapped 3/3 Construct Token means the opponent can block and kill Emperor for free. Emperor of Bones is a key value engine that can reanimate exiled creatures. The Eldrazi Spawn (0/1) deals 0 damage even if unblocked. The player's reasoning incorrectly assumed they had Nethergoyf and other creatures on the board that aren't actually there.

The player declined to activate Emry, Lurker of the Loch's ability, which would have allowed them to cast an artifact from their graveyard (such as Mishra's Bauble for card advantage, Haywire Mite for interaction, or Tormod's Crypt). Emry's tap ability is a pure-upside ability that costs nothing but tapping the creature - there's no reason to decline it. The player's reasoning was confused, citing bugs and weird timeline issues rather than evaluating the game state. Additionally, they had Urza's Saga on chapter II which could create a Construct token, giving them more board presence. The 'After' line shows Urza's Saga actually triggered its chapter III search, meaning the Saga was about to be sacrificed - making the Construct activation even more valuable as it was the last chance to use it. Declining both pure-upside activated abilities with no downside is a clear mistake.

Declined to activate Emry's tap ability when there are multiple high-value 0-cost artifacts in the graveyard (Mishra's Bauble for free card draw, Tormod's Crypt to counter Emperor of Bones' graveyard recursion). The player's reasoning incorrectly assumed Tormod's Crypt was already on the battlefield/stack when it was actually in the graveyard.

Shadowspear is on the stack being cast by Haiku Spike. This is a powerful equipment that gives +1/+1, trample, and lifelink, and can remove hexproof/indestructible. Gem25F Valley has Metallic Rebuke available with enough artifacts to cast it cheaply (Mox Opal, Mox Amber, Construct Token, plus lands = easily improvise the cost). With Haiku Spike at 12 life and having Emperor of Bones on board, letting Shadowspear resolve gives the opponent's creatures lifelink and makes racing harder. Additionally, Pithing Needle is already on the battlefield (likely naming something important), so Shadowspear adds significant value to Haiku Spike's board.

Playing Scalding Tarn instead of Urza's Saga delays the Saga's progression by a full turn. With 3+ artifacts already on board (Mox Opal, Mox Amber, Construct Token), Urza's Saga would create large Construct tokens and eventually tutor for a key artifact. The player already has abundant colored mana sources and doesn't need the Tarn's fixing right now.

Casting Cori-Steel Cutter (a non-creature artifact equipment) before combat is suboptimal sequencing. The Construct Token is already on the battlefield and could attack. More importantly, casting Cori-Steel Cutter before using Emry's tap ability wastes the opportunity to potentially recur a more impactful artifact from the graveyard first. Additionally, casting a spell precombat when holding Metallic Rebuke (a counterspell) and having no urgent need to deploy the equipment telegraphs information unnecessarily. The player should have activated Emry first to see what artifact they could recur (e.g., Aether Spellbomb to bounce Nethergoyf before combat), then attacked, then cast Cori-Steel Cutter post-combat if desired.

With Haiku Spike at 12 life and only a 1/2 Nethergoyf and 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn as potential blockers (all lands tapped, no tricks available), attacking with just the 4/4 Construct leaves 4-5 damage on the table. Sending both Construct and Quantum Riddler forces opponent to only block one, guaranteeing at least 4 damage gets through instead of risking a chump block on the solo Construct.

chosen_display: Ifnir Deadlands — {2}{B}{B}, {T}, Sacrifice a Desert: Put two -1/-1... [Activate]
annotation_description: Haiku Spike activated Ifnir Deadlands without first playing the Ifnir Deadlands from hand. Playing the land first would provide an additional mana source and keep a Desert on the battlefield for future use, while still allowing the activation with the on-board copy.

Attacking with Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1) deals 0 damage while giving up a potential chump blocker at 4 life. The opponent has a Construct Token and Quantum Riddler that will untap next turn and could threaten lethal.

Fetched Steam Vents instead of Island when there's no need for red mana this turn or in the foreseeable future. The opponent is at 4 life with all permanents tapped, and Quantum Riddler (4/6 flying) attacks for exact lethal. Paying 2 extra life for Steam Vents is unnecessary.

Only attacked with Quantum Riddler (5/7) instead of both creatures when going for lethal. While Riddler alone deals lethal (5 > 4 life) and opponent appears tapped out, attacking with both Quantum Riddler and Construct Token (4/4) is strictly better as it plays around any possible instant-speed interaction that could save the opponent.
